rates_fed: Fed expectations are holding fairly steady with the market pricing in roughly 33 basis points of rate hikes over the final two meetings of the year, with about 50/50 odds of a hike at the October 28th meeting, and an additional 35 basis points of increases priced in for 2027. Kansas City Fed President Schmid warned Friday that elevated inflation is being driven by more than just oil, and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari echoed those hawkish sentiments Sunday morning. The BOJ's recent rate hike was slightly more dovish than expected, but globally monetary policy remains pointed in a hawkish direction with the BOJ, ECB, and FOMC all hiking this month. Treasury plans to issue over $1 trillion in T-bills over the next 12 months, pushing bills above 24% of marketable debt and above the Treasury's own 20% target.
market_outlook: Adam's lean is cautiously bullish for Monday, driven almost entirely by diplomatic optimism surrounding the UN General Assembly and the possibility of Iran-related de-escalation, which could crack oil prices lower and unleash a cascade of favorable macro effects. The key catalyst to watch is any headline out of the UN General Assembly suggesting diplomatic progress on the Middle East or Iran, as well as the Trump/Xi summit Thursday.
bull_case: Nearly all of the market's macro problems can be traced back to oil, and even a minor geopolitical improvement could trigger an outsized drop in energy prices, with knock-on benefits including lower yields, reduced inflation, better corporate margins, and improved consumer confidence. The UN General Assembly running September 22-28 in New York brings together officials from multiple Middle Eastern countries including Iran, creating a genuine window for diplomatic progress. Trump reportedly called off planned air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute and expressed openness to meeting Iran's president, suggesting a negotiated off-ramp may be possible. China and Pakistan are reportedly urging Iran to rein in the Houthis, a sign global pressure is building.
bear_case: The geopolitical landscape remains genuinely grim — Iran is tightening its grip on global energy supplies via the Strait of Hormuz, aligned militias in Iraq, and the Houthis in Yemen who dramatically escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia over the weekend. The economy and corporate earnings have held up well over the summer, but the latest spike in energy prices will begin working through the system soon and could trigger meaningful demand destruction. The AI sector faces fresh headwinds including a delayed Anthropic IPO, underwhelming Anthropic 2027 ARR projections, OpenAI's staggering projected negative free cash flow of $280 billion through 2030, and Oracle data center debt stress. UN General Assembly diplomatic optimism may simply turn out to be wishful thinking.

The company appears to be successfully trading down on price to maintain volume while competitors struggle. This is a relative positive for Disney at a time when consumer discretionary spending faces macro pressure.

Novo Nordisk shares are slumping in European trading after the company failed to provide sufficiently granular financial targets at its Monday analyst meeting. Investors were disappointed by the lack of specificity despite the company touting future blockbuster launches. The stock is underperforming the broader European market rally.

Oracle was the subject of a negative FT report over the weekend focused on poor price action in debt tied to a massive Oracle-linked data center in New Mexico known as Project Jupiter. Efforts to offload loans tied to the facility have reportedly hit a wall, raising fresh concerns about Oracle's off-balance sheet data center exposure. This adds to a broader negative AI infrastructure narrative over the weekend.

Paramount is in advanced settlement talks with California's attorney general to resolve a lawsuit against its Warner Bros. Discovery merger, with Paramount potentially agreeing to preserve CNN's editorial independence and divest certain cable channels including Comedy Central. However, not all state attorneys general involved are on board, keeping the deal's completion uncertain. The talks suggest the merger is inching closer to regulatory clearance but faces remaining hurdles.

Results will be closely watched as a read on consumer spending health at a time when macro headwinds from energy prices and inflation are intensifying. tts_summary:
Good morning. Here's what you need to know heading into Monday September 21st.

Futures are rallying despite a weekend loaded with negative headlines. S&P is up about 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq is up 110 basis points, and the Russell 2000 is up 47 basis points. Asia closed broadly higher and Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points. Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve. Brent crude is sliding 170 basis points to around 102 dollars and 10 cents. Bitcoin is surging 350 basis points to roughly 83,890 dollars.

So why are stocks rallying when the news flow was almost entirely negative? The primary driver is diplomatic optimism around this week's UN General Assembly in New York. Trump said he would be open to meeting with Iran's president, who is expected to attend. He also reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. Markets are betting that even a small improvement in Middle East tensions could crack oil prices sharply lower, and if that happens, you get a cascade of bullish knock-on effects — lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, better margins, and improved consumer confidence. That is the bull case in one sentence.

The bear case is that this is wishful thinking. The Houthis dramatically escalated their attacks on Saudi Arabia over the weekend. Iran is tightening its grip on Hormuz and aligned militias across the region. Ukraine launched its largest drone strike of the war against Russia. The geopolitical picture is genuinely bad, and energy prices are going to start working their way through corporate earnings quickly.

On the Fed, the market is pricing in roughly 33 basis points of hikes over the final two meetings of the year, with about 50/50 odds at the October 28th meeting. Kansas City Fed President Schmid and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari both made hawkish comments over the weekend warning that inflation is spreading beyond energy. The BOJ, ECB, and FOMC all hiked this month. The global monetary policy backdrop remains firmly hawkish.

On individual names — Oracle is under pressure after an FT report that debt tied to its massive New Mexico data center, known as Project Jupiter, has hit a wall with lenders. That lands in the middle of a broader AI infrastructure reset this weekend, which also included delayed Anthropic IPO news, disappointing Anthropic 2027 revenue projections, and OpenAI projecting negative free cash flow of 280 billion dollars through 2030. AI capex sentiment is clearly under scrutiny.

Novo Nordisk is lower in European trading after disappointing investors at its analyst meeting by not providing granular enough financial targets. Disney's parks business is a positive standout, outperforming peers by using price promotions to drive traffic. Paramount and Warner are in advanced settlement talks with California around their merger, though not all state attorneys general are aligned yet.

Looking ahead this week, the big events are the UN General Assembly running through September 28th, the Trump and Xi summit on Thursday, and the US flash PMIs Wednesday morning. Costco reports Thursday night. Meta's Zuckerberg keynotes the Connect conference Wednesday at 7pm Eastern. Watch any Iran or Middle East headline closely — that is the swing factor for the entire market right now.
